name: subroutine
description: A self-hosted, agent-native task and decision tracker for people and coding agents working on complex projects. Wires this session to a Subroutine instance and carries the working practice for using it well. Nothing to install first: it starts Subroutine through 'uvx', which fetches and caches it on first use — so you need uv on your machine (astral.sh/uv) and nothing else. If you have already run 'uv tool install subroutine', that copy is used instead. It starts a program on your own machine, so it works in Claude Code and the desktop apps and not on the web.

connection.title: Which instance (optional)
connection.description: The name of a connection you have already configured, such as 'work'. Leave this empty for your default connection — the database on this machine, unless you have set 'default_connection' to something else. Run 'subroutine connections' to see the names and which one that is. Note that one session reaches one instance, so if you keep work and personal instances separately, name the one this project belongs to. Connections are set up with 'subroutine' itself, not here.

workspace.title: Which workspace (optional)
workspace.description: The workspace this session's work belongs in, by its short name — 'subroutine list' prints them beside each item when there is more than one. Leave empty if the credential this session uses reaches only one, which is the usual case: it is then resolved for you and naming it here would be a word you never needed. Where it reaches two or more, an agent that has not been told a name has every read refused as ambiguous, and no way to learn one. This is a default rather than a limit — a call may still name another, and a token pinned to a workspace is what narrows access for real.

token.title: Agent token (optional)
token.description: A token for this plugin's tools alone, for when an agent here should have less access than you do. Usually leave it empty: 'subroutine agent create <name> --store' gives the agent an account of its own and stores its token on the connection, and a Claude Code session then uses it for the tools and for the commands the agent runs alike. A token entered here reaches the tools only, so an agent that also runs commands would be itself half the time and you the other half, silently. Leave it empty with nothing stored to act as you. Your editor stores this, not Subroutine, and where it puts it depends on the editor and the machine - on Windows it is a file under your home directory. Treat it as you would any password there.
